flashcards.front: What is the primary threat vector for AI-Powered Threat Detection?
flashcards.back_definition: Adversaries exploit traditional static signature rules on SIEM network traffic to bypass standard perimeter security controls.
flashcards.back_example: Example: SIEM Anomaly: Outlier exfiltration rate detected (12.4 GB/hour)
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse this threat with other layers (like physical breaches or certificate revocations) which target different assets.
flashcards.back_hook: Recall: traditional static signature rules is the unlocked door; SIEM network traffic is what the attacker wants to steal.

flashcards.front: How does the security team mitigate AI-Powered Threat Detection threats?
flashcards.back_definition: Deploying and enforcing defensive machine learning baselines directly hardens SIEM network traffic and blocks unauthorized connections.
flashcards.back_example: Action: Update security configurations to require defensive machine learning baselines.
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse mitigation (actively blocking the exploit) with detection (simply logging or alerting the event).
flashcards.back_hook: Mitigation is the shield; detection is the security camera.

flashcards.front: How do analysts detect exploitation of AI-Powered Threat Detection?
flashcards.back_definition: By auditing event data and implementing logic flags built to alert on dynamic traffic volume deviations.
flashcards.back_example: Syslog trace: SIEM Anomaly: Outlier exfiltration rate detected (12.4 GB/hour)
flashcards.back_confusion: Don't confuse signature-based detection (matching known strings) with anomaly-based detection (mapping dynamic standard deviations).
flashcards.back_hook: Detection is looking for the fingerprint left behind by the threat.
